annotation_description: Playing Multiversal Passage on turn 1 requires paying 2 life to have it enter untapped, or it enters tapped. Starting Town enters untapped for free on turns 1-3 and can produce any color of mana (at the cost of 1 life per activation for colored mana). Since the player has a turn 2 play (Badgermole Cub at {1}{G} or Explosive Prodigy at {1}{R}), they want untapped mana on both turns. Playing Starting Town first (free untapped) and Multiversal Passage second (paying 2 life for untapped, or accepting tapped if not needed immediately) would save 2 life if they need Multiversal Passage untapped on turn 2, or is equivalent if they pay life for both. More importantly, Starting Town produces any color, which is more flexible on turn 1. Playing Multiversal Passage first means choosing a basic land type now and potentially paying 2 life, when Starting Town would have entered untapped for free.

Casting Sleight of Hand before playing a land is a sequencing error. DSV3 Analyst has Multiversal Passage and two Riverpyre Verges in hand. Playing a land first costs nothing and preserves options — Sleight of Hand could reveal information that affects which land to play, but more importantly, playing a land first keeps mana open. Specifically, if they play Multiversal Passage (paying 2 life for untapped) or a Riverpyre Verge, they could have 2 mana available after casting Sleight of Hand, potentially leaving up Spell Snare or Bounce Off. By casting Sleight of Hand first, they use their only mana and can only play a tapped land afterward with no mana open. However, Riverpyre Verge only produces U if you control an Island or Mountain, and Multiversal Passage could be set to Island but costs 2 life. The correct sequencing is to play the land first, then cast Sleight of Hand with the information of what lands you have available, potentially leaving up interaction.

Bouncing Badgermole Cub instead of the earthbent Multiversal Passage (which is a land creature) misses a significant tempo opportunity. Bouncing the animated land would set the opponent back a land drop (from 2 lands to 1), essentially acting as both removal and land destruction. The opponent would need to use their next land drop just to replay Multiversal Passage. Meanwhile, the Badgermole Cub can simply be replayed next turn for 1G, and its ETB will earthbend yet another land, potentially gaining even more value than before.

Casting Formidable Speaker on turn 3 is suboptimal compared to Badgermole Cub. Badgermole Cub costs only 2 mana (leaving 1 mana open), creates an additional creature via earthbend, and its mana-doubling ability on tapped creatures synergizes with future plays. Formidable Speaker's ETB requires discarding a card to tutor, which is fine, but the opponent has 2 cards in graveyard (instants/sorceries) and could have Spell Snare ready (counters MV 2 spells) - though both are MV 2 so both are vulnerable. More importantly, Badgermole Cub on turn 2-equivalent mana with earthbend creates board presence and ramp, while Formidable Speaker without a clear discard target is just a 2/4 body. The Speaker is better if you have something worth discarding to tutor for, but the hand has strong cards already. Additionally, casting a creature before combat when holding no combat tricks is a minor sequencing issue but largely irrelevant with no attackers.

Nature's Rhythm costs XGG, and with 4 lands available, the player can only pay X=2 at most (2 generic + GG). However, the player hasn't specified X yet - this is just selecting the spell. The bigger issue is that casting Nature's Rhythm with X=2 uses all 4 mana to search for a 2-mana-or-less creature, when they already have Badgermole Cub (a solid 2-drop) in hand. Meanwhile, the opponent has 3 lands with blue mana open and already has Bounce Off and Sleight of Hand in graveyard, meaning Eddymurk Crab costs less and they likely have countermagic available. Casting Badgermole Cub for 2 mana would develop the board while leaving 2 mana open, and the earthbend trigger would create additional board presence. Using Nature's Rhythm to tutor a creature when you already have playable creatures in hand and the opponent likely has interaction is wasteful - especially tapping out into open blue mana.

Explosive Prodigy is a 1/1 for 1R that deals X damage where X is the number of colors among permanents you control. Currently the player controls green permanents (Formidable Speaker, Hushwood Verge) and colorless lands, so X would be 1 at best - dealing 1 damage to nothing since the opponent has no creatures. The ability has no valid target. Meanwhile, Badgermole Cub (2/2 for 1G) would be a better play - it earthbends a land (creating a creature with a +1/+1 counter) and provides mana acceleration when tapping creatures for mana. This develops the board much more effectively. Alternatively, casting Mockingbird for X=2 (paying 1UG or similar) to copy Formidable Speaker would also be strong. Explosive Prodigy's ETB trigger has no valid target since the opponent controls no creatures, making it just a 1/1 body.

Player passed their entire precombat main phase without casting any spells despite having 4 mana available and multiple strong plays in hand. The reasoning was confused, referencing Explosive Prodigy's ability when the actual choices were to cast creatures or activate Formidable Speaker. The opponent has an empty board with only 3 lands, making this a perfect window to develop.
Activated Formidable Speaker's untap ability at the end of their own turn to untap Hushwood Verge, which would naturally untap during the untap step anyway. This spent 1 mana for zero benefit.

DSV3 Analyst chose not to play a land on turn 4, missing a land drop. They have three lands to choose from (Multiversal Passage, Steam Vents, Riverpyre Verge) and only 3 lands on the battlefield. Playing a 4th land is important for casting Eddymurk Crab sooner (which costs 7 but is reduced by instants/sorceries in graveyard - currently 2, so it costs 5). Getting to 4 mana also allows holding up Spider-Sense plus Spell Snare. There is no reason to skip a land drop here.

Llama4 Truth has 5 lands (Multiversal Passage/Forest, Starting Town, Starting Town, Hushwood Verge, plus Formidable Speaker on board) and a hand full of castable creatures, but chose to pass without casting anything. They have the mana to cast Badgermole Cub (1G) and Spider Manifestation (1R/G) in the same turn, or at minimum should cast one creature to develop the board. The opponent has only 3 lands and no board presence - this is the time to build pressure. Passing an entire turn with 5 mana available and multiple cheap creatures in hand wastes significant tempo.

Attacking with Formidable Speaker (2/4) into an opponent with 3 open lands (including Riverpyre Verge for blue mana) and Eddymurk Crab potentially castable (costs 7 but reduced by instants/sorceries in graveyard - they have 2, so it costs 5, and they only have 3 lands so not yet). More importantly, Formidable Speaker has a tap ability ({1}, {T}: Untap another target permanent) that could be valuable to keep available. Attacking with it means losing the ability to use it during the opponent's turn or to untap a land for mana. The 2 damage is marginal at 20 life. Additionally, attacking with Multiversal Passage (an earthbent land that's a 1/1 creature) risks losing a land if the opponent has removal. With only Bounce Off and Sleight of Hand in graveyard, the opponent could have drawn into instant-speed removal. However, the opponent has no creatures to block with, so the attacks do connect for 3 damage safely. The risk is relatively low but the Formidable Speaker tap could have been kept available.

DSV3 Analyst has 8 cards in hand and 3 lands on the battlefield. They need to play a land this turn to develop their mana and avoid missing a land drop. They have multiple land options available (Island, Multiversal Passage, Steam Vents, Riverpyre Verge) and chose not to play any of them. Missing a land drop on turn 5 when holding lands is a clear mistake, especially when they have Eddymurk Crab in hand that costs 7 mana (reduced by instants/sorceries in graveyard). They also have 8 cards in hand and will need to discard to hand size if they don't play something.

DSV3 Analyst has 3 lands on the battlefield and 8 cards in hand. It's their postcombat main phase, and they need to play a land to avoid discarding down to 7. They have multiple land options (Island, Multiversal Passage, Steam Vents, Riverpyre Verge) and chose not to play any of them. This means they'll have to discard a card for no reason, losing a card's worth of value. Playing a 4th land would also help cast Eddymurk Crab sooner (which costs 7 minus graveyard instants/sorceries, currently 2 in graveyard = 5 mana needed).

DSV3 Analyst discarded Multiversal Passage (a dual land that could enter as any basic type) instead of a redundant Spell Snare or Riverpyre Verge. With only 3 lands on the battlefield and needing to reach 5-7 mana to cast Eddymurk Crab (which costs 7 but is reduced by instants/sorceries in graveyard), every land matters. Multiversal Passage is strictly better than a basic Island since it can be any basic land type, and the player already has an Island in hand. Meanwhile, having two Spell Snares is redundant since they only counter 2-mana spells, and the opponent may not have many targets. The reasoning even mentions considering discarding Eddymurk Crab or a land, but then discards one of their best lands.

Llama4 Truth has 4 mana available (Multiversal Passage, 2x Starting Town, Hushwood Verge) plus Formidable Speaker can tap for mana via untap shenanigans. They passed without casting anything despite having multiple strong plays. Badgermole Cub (1G) would earthbend a land creating another creature, Spider Manifestation (1R/G, castable with green) would add a mana dork and 2/2 reach body, and they could potentially cast multiple spells this turn. The opponent has only 3 lands and no board presence - this is the time to develop. Passing the entire main phase with a full hand of castable spells wastes significant tempo.

Llama4 Truth has a 2/4 Formidable Speaker and a 1/1 Multiversal Passage (earthbent land with a +1/+1 counter) on board against an opponent with no creatures and only 3 lands (no blockers). The opponent is at 17 life. Attacking with at least the Formidable Speaker (2 damage) and possibly the Multiversal Passage (1 damage) would deal free damage with zero risk since the opponent has no blockers. Instead, the player skipped the attack entirely, missing 2-3 points of free damage.

Llama4 Truth has 5 lands (Multiversal Passage tapped, 2 Starting Towns, Formidable Speaker tapped, Hushwood Verge) with at least 2-3 untapped lands available. They could cast Badgermole Cub (1G) to develop the board with a 2/2 and earthbend a land into a creature, or Spider Manifestation (1R/G) for a 2/2 reach + mana dork. The opponent has only 3 lands and no creatures. Passing the turn with untapped mana and multiple castable creatures wastes tempo against an opponent who is clearly holding up countermagic/interaction. However, with the opponent at 3 lands and 2 instants/sorceries in graveyard, they could have Spell Snare (counters MV2) or Spider-Sense. Even so, deploying at least one threat is better than doing nothing - if they counter it, that's still trading resources favorably since Llama4 has a full hand of 7 cards. Passing with a full hand and available mana is a significant tempo loss.

Playing Steam Vents instead of Island when they already have red mana available from Spirebluff Canal and Riverpyre Verge. Their hand is almost entirely blue spells (Spider-Sense, Spell Snare x2, Eddymurk Crab). Island provides the same blue mana without costing 2 life (if entering untapped) or tempo (if entering tapped). Steam Vents' Island Mountain typing doesn't provide additional enablement since they already have an Island in play.

Llama4 Truth has 5 lands (including Hushwood Verge for green and Multiversal Passage likely set to Forest/green), 8 cards in hand, and chose to do nothing on turn 7. They have multiple strong plays available: Badgermole Cub (1G) with earthbend to animate a land, Spider Manifestation (1R/G) as a mana dork that enables bigger plays, or even Nature's Rhythm to tutor a creature onto the battlefield. With the opponent at 15 life and only 4 lands with no board presence, this is a critical window to develop the board. Passing without casting anything wastes an entire turn of development against an opponent who likely has countermagic but can't counter everything.

Explosive Prodigy's ETB deals damage to a target creature an opponent controls, but the opponent has NO creatures on the battlefield. This makes it essentially a vanilla 1/1 for 2 mana. Meanwhile, Spider Manifestation is a 2/2 reach mana dork that would accelerate toward casting Nature's Rhythm, and Badgermole Cub creates an additional creature via earthbend.

DSV3 Analyst has 5 lands (Spirebluff Canal, Island, Riverpyre Verge, Steam Vents, Island) producing up to 4U and 2R (or various combinations). Eddymurk Crab costs {5}{U}{U} = 7 mana, but it costs {1} less for each instant/sorcery in graveyard. With Sleight of Hand, Bounce Off, and Multiversal Passage in graveyard — wait, Multiversal Passage is a land, not instant/sorcery. So 2 instant/sorcery cards (Sleight of Hand, Bounce Off) reduce the cost by 2, making it {3}{U}{U} = 5 mana total. With 5 lands available, DSV3 Analyst could have cast Eddymurk Crab at flash speed during combat to tap Formidable Speaker (the attacker) and potentially another creature. This would have effectively neutralized the attack and put a 5/5 body on the board. Instead, they passed and took 2 damage from the unblocked Formidable Speaker.

With 6 untapped lands and the opponent at 7 life with only a tapped 5/5, casting Nature's Rhythm for X=4 would put a creature with MV 4 or less directly onto the battlefield from the library, which is significantly more impactful than a 2/2 Badgermole Cub. The earthbend haste token from Badgermole Cub is nice but doesn't compare to tutoring the best creature in the deck directly into play.

Chose to earthbend Breeding Pool, one of the most valuable lands (dual G/U, only reliable blue source for Mockingbird in hand), instead of a less important land like Hushwood Verge or an untapped Starting Town. Since earthbend makes the land into a creature that's vulnerable to removal, risking the blue source is unnecessary.

Llama4 Truth only attacked with Breeding Pool (a 1/1 animated land) when Badgermole Cub (2/2) was also available to attack. The opponent is at 7 life with their only creature (Eddymurk Crab) tapped, so there are no blockers. Attacking with both Breeding Pool and Badgermole Cub would deal 3 damage instead of 1, bringing the opponent to 4 life instead of 6. With Explosive Prodigy in hand (which deals damage based on colors among permanents), getting the opponent lower is critical. Missing 2 extra damage against a defenseless opponent at 7 life is a significant missed opportunity.

Chose Island for Multiversal Passage when they already have Breeding Pool providing blue mana. With Nature's Rhythm requiring GG and being the most impactful card in hand, Forest would have been more useful. Forest would also enable Hushwood Verge to produce white mana. The only blue card in hand is Mockingbird which needs generic + U, already covered by Breeding Pool.

Player appears confused about whose turn it is and likely passed without attacking. The opponent is at 6 life with only Eddymurk Crab (5/5) as a blocker. By casting Spider Manifestation (2 mana) first, then attacking with all 5 creatures (1+2+1+2+2=8 power), the Crab can only block one creature, and the remaining attackers deal at least 6 damage regardless of blocking assignment — that's exactly lethal.

Opponent is at 6 life with a 5/5 Eddymurk Crab as blocker. Attacking with all 4 creatures (total 6 power) means the Crab can block any attacker, reducing damage below 6 and preventing lethal. However, casting Spider Manifestation (2/2 for 2 mana, easily affordable) before combat would give 8 total power across 5 attackers. Even with the Crab blocking any one creature, at least 6 damage gets through for lethal.

At 6 life facing multiple attackers, DSV3 Analyst could have used Spider-Sense with web-slinging to bounce their tapped Eddymurk Crab (countering the low-value Sleight of Hand for just {U}), then replayed Eddymurk Crab on their main phase untapped, using its ETB to tap two of the opponent's creatures. This would provide critical defensive tempo.

Playing Steam Vents (which enters tapped to preserve life at 6hp) instead of Riverpyre Verge, which would enter untapped for free since they already control Islands and Mountains. This costs them one available mana this turn for holding up countermagic like Spell Pierce or Spider-Sense.

Tapping Formidable Speaker (2/4) to untap Breeding Pool during combat removes a 2-power attacker against an opponent at 6 life. The extra mana could enable post-combat plays, but every point of damage matters when the opponent is this low. Attacking with all three creatures (Formidable Speaker + Badgermole Cub + Multiversal Passage = 5 power) forces the opponent to make tough blocking decisions with Eddymurk Crab.

Blocked with Badgermole Cub (a valuable creature with mana-doubling ability) instead of an earthbend land creature. The earthbend lands (Multiversal Passage or Breeding Pool) return to the battlefield tapped when they die, making them ideal chump blockers that cost nothing permanent. Badgermole Cub's ability to add additional {G} when tapping creatures for mana synergizes with the Spider Manifestations in hand.

Casting Llanowar Elves in precombat main phase when it doesn't affect combat math. The opponent's Eddymurk Crab is tapped and can't block, so attacking first with Formidable Speaker and the animated Multiversal Passage is free damage. Playing creatures before combat unnecessarily gives the opponent information and risks the creature being relevant to counterplay.

The opponent is at 6 life. Llama4 Truth has Formidable Speaker (2/4) on the board, but it's tapped. Breeding Pool is a land that was earthbent into a creature (from Badgermole Cub's ability earlier). The player chose to attack with only Breeding Pool (likely a 1/1 with a +1/+1 counter, so 1/1) instead of selecting 'All attack' which would send all available creatures. With the opponent at 6 life, maximizing attackers is critical. Formidable Speaker is tapped so it can't attack regardless, but Multiversal Passage (the untapped one) might also be an earthbent land-creature. By not choosing 'All attack', the player potentially missed sending all available creatures and reducing the opponent's life total more aggressively. More critically, the player has Explosive Prodigy in hand which deals damage equal to colors among permanents controlled - this could have been used as burn to finish the opponent. The player also has two Nature's Rhythm to tutor threats. Attacking with just one creature when the opponent is at 6 life and you have multiple potential attackers is a significant missed opportunity.

With 4 untapped lands available, Llama4 only cast Explosive Prodigy (2 mana) when they could have also cast Spider Manifestation (2 mana) in the same turn, developing more board presence with the opponent at 5 life. Additionally, casting Spider Manifestation first would have potentially increased the color count for Explosive Prodigy's Vivid trigger. The Explosive Prodigy's damage likely doesn't kill the 5/5 Eddymurk Crab anyway, making the sequencing and mana usage suboptimal.

DSV3 Analyst cast Sleight of Hand before playing a land. They have Riverpyre Verge and Spirebluff Canal in hand. Spirebluff Canal would enter tapped (they control more than 2 other lands), but Riverpyre Verge could tap for U or R since they control Islands and Mountains. Playing the land first preserves more mana options and doesn't cost anything. Additionally, casting Sleight of Hand adds a sorcery to the graveyard, which would reduce Eddymurk Crab's cost by 1 more — but they should still play the land first to have maximum mana available after the Sleight resolves, in case they want to cast what they find. With 5 life and needing to deploy threats while holding up countermagic, sequencing land before spell is strictly better here.

The opponent is at 5 life. Multiversal Passage (1/1 animated land) and Formidable Speaker (2/4) together deal exactly 3 damage. The Eddymurk Crab is tapped, and the opponent has all lands tapped except two untapped Steam Vents (so 2 mana available). Attacking with both creatures deals 3 damage, putting opponent to 2. But the player only selected Multiversal Passage as an attacker, not both creatures. The reasoning says 'attack with Multiversal Passage and Formidable Speaker' but only Multiversal Passage was chosen. Even attacking with both only deals 3, not lethal, but every point of damage matters at 5 life. Missing 2 damage from Formidable Speaker is significant when the opponent is at 5 life.

At 4 life vs opponent's 13, attacking with only one Eddymurk Crab instead of both. The opponent has only Gene Pollinator (1/2) as an untapped potential blocker, so attacking with both would likely deal 8-10 damage (opponent to 3-5). At 4 life, the game needs to end quickly, and the clock difference between a 2-turn kill and a 3+ turn kill is significant.

At 4 life, Multiversal Passage either enters tapped (losing an untapped mana source) or costs 2 precious life. Island enters untapped for free, which is important for holding up counterspells (Spider-Sense, Spell Snare, Spell Pierce) on the opponent's turn.

message: Select an instant spell, sorcery spell, or triggered ability
annotation_description: DSV3 Analyst cast Spider-Sense targeting its own Spider-Sense on the stack. Spider-Sense counters target instant spell, sorcery spell, or triggered ability - by targeting itself, it counters itself, accomplishing absolutely nothing and wasting the card. The choice presented was between 'Ability' (presumably some triggered ability on the stack) and 'Spider-Sense' itself. If there was a triggered ability on the stack (likely from Badgermole Cub's earthbend or similar), countering that ability would have been the correct play to deny the opponent value.

With two 5/5 Eddymurk Crabs available and opponent at 8 life with only a 2/2 Badgermole Cub as a blocker, attacking with both crabs forces at least 5 damage through (opponent to 3) or delivers lethal 10 if unblocked. Attacking with only one crab means at most 5 damage and misses the potential lethal.

Opponent is at 4 HP with only one blocker (Eddymurk Crab 5/5). Attacking with only Badgermole Cub means the opponent can block it and take 0 damage, or not block and take 2. Attacking with both Badgermole Cub and Starting Town (earthbent land creature) would force at least 1 damage through since the Crab can only block one, and the land returns to battlefield if it dies due to earthbend.

At 3 life vs opponent's 4 life with no creatures on board, leading with Gene Pollinator (1/2) is less impactful than Spider Manifestation (2/2 that also taps for mana). More importantly, with 7 mana available, the player should be deploying multiple creatures this turn to maximize pressure since the opponent is at 4 life.

Player is confused about whose turn it is during their own precombat main phase, thinking the opponent is declaring attackers when they should be selecting their own attackers. With opponent at 4 life, this is a critical turn where attacking and potentially following up with Explosive Prodigy or Spider Manifestation could set up or achieve lethal. The confused reasoning likely led to not attacking or attacking suboptimally.
